analysis: Reviewed .github/scripts/test-threat-budget.py (base text only, lines 1-1083; head additions seen only via patch excerpt). The change is test-only CI tooling for an offline threat-review harness. Changes are: renaming and tightening test_cross_file_uncertainty at lines 664/671 (expects [SONNET, SONNET] instead of [SONNET, SONNET, OPUS], with manual_review_reasons still non-empty and clean() still false); and adding new tests after line 948 (manual GitHub rerun hands off with MANUAL_SCAN_RERUN_DISABLED, zero paid calls, no source collection, clean() false; scanner runtime bound of fifty minutes). Nothing in this file touches the provider, coordinator WebSocket, attestation, App Attest, key custody, prefix cache (T-041) or fan helper assets, so no provider threat IDs are implicated. The security-relevant behavior is in the unseen production modules (threat_review.budget_runner, budget_scan, merge_policy), which are not supplied. The tests assert fail-closed properties: uncertainty still blocks merge (clean false) even though local Opus rescan is removed, and reruns spend nothing and cannot be marked clean. Remaining question for integration: whether the production code in other files actually implements these semantics, notably that dropping the redundant local rescan does not leave unresolved uncertainty considered clean, and that the rerun gate cannot be bypassed by GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT manipulation. The patch excerpt is truncated (patch_excerpt_complete=false), so the second new test body was not fully visible. No findings.
